nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You find her in the center of the refugee camp, kneeling in the mud beside a man whose leg has gone the color of old bark. She doesn't look up.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: Don't step on the moss poultice. Took me an hour to cultivate.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: You're standing there with weapons on your hips and I've got seventeen people who can't walk. Whatever you're selling, I'm not buying it today.

choices.text: We're not selling anything. We need your help.
The blight is spreading north. You know that better than anyone.

nodes.speaker: player
nodes.text: We're not selling anything. We need your help.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: At least you're direct. Half the people who come through here want something and spend twenty minutes not saying what it is.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: Doesn't change the answer. I have people here who need me.

nodes.speaker: player
nodes.text: The blight is spreading north. You know that better than anyone.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: I've been watching the root-lines for three weeks. The gray rot hit the eastern fen last month. The herons left the marshes two days ago.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: Herons don't leave. Not unless the water's already dead.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You say nothing. You watch her work. Her hands move without hesitation — pressing, folding, binding. She knows what she's doing. She's done it a thousand times.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: You're still there.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: Most warriors get bored after thirty seconds. They want to be doing something loud.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: Fine. Say what you came to say.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: I don't trust warriors. I've stitched too many people back together after warriors decided something. No offense.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: But I can smell it on the wind. The blight. It's not staying in the lowlands anymore.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: Something is pushing it. Something with intent.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: Wait.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: You. In the back. You've been running your own field triage since you got here, haven't you. The woman with the light magic.

nodes.speaker: hannah
nodes.text: The man by the cart had a wound that needed closing. I closed it.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: You didn't waste the light on his pain. Just the infection.

nodes.speaker: hannah
nodes.text: Pain is survivable. Infection isn't.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: Hm.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: You have anyone in your group who heals? Actually heals, not just waves a wand and hopes?

nodes.speaker: player
nodes.text: We manage.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: That's not a yes.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: These people will be stable by morning. The village has two others who know basic wound-craft. They don't need me standing over them.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: What they need — what everyone in this swamp needs — is for whatever is killing the root-lines to stop.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: I don't like parties. I don't like noise. I don't like people who make decisions with swords before they've thought for five seconds.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: But someone has to go. Might as well be someone who knows which end of a root is poisoned.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: I'm not a soldier. I won't do things because you say so. I'll do things because they need doing.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: That agreeable to you?

nodes.speaker: player
nodes.text: That's agreeable.

nodes.speaker: druidess
nodes.text: Good. Give me until dawn. I want to finish the poultice.
